R01-interface-wetting-v1.target: Explain formation and persistence of internal cavities and generate a discriminating prediction; do not treat f(t) as a concentration.
known_relations: E01: B mean empty-area fraction increases across 0, 4, 8, 12, 24 h; A falls to a low plateau-like value. There are seven fields per condition but only two independent preparations; field/object summaries do not provide preparation-level uncertainty.

E02: length-separated template fractions M, M+L, M+S have different single-endpoint cavity fractions (approximately 0.000028, 0.0445, 0.0941 as reported medians); this is association in a distinct endpoint preparation, not a causal mixture series or time course.
E03: motion summaries differ by condition but are affected by unequal track counts/durations and contain no same-object cavity area or appearance/disappearance labels.

E04: three measured tie lines contain reference and variant RNA concentrations in dilute/dense phases; measured concentrations do not map to cavities and lack phase volumes, B RNA proportions, or time-resolved yield.
E05: B has a 0.9466 reference DNA read fraction and listed non-reference reads; DNA frequencies do not determine RNA concentrations or expression proportions.

hypotheses.statement: A minority RNA species X produced from a non-reference template preferentially adsorbs to the internal phase boundary and lowers its effective interfacial free energy. Once a cavity nucleates, this boundary enrichment reduces the energetic cost of maintaining it, so cavity persistence can increase even when the bulk dense phase remains connected.
assumptions: At least one transcribed non-reference RNA species exists in B; not inferred quantitatively from DNA reads.
An internal phase boundary with distinguishable adjacent regions exists.
X has a measurable affinity for that boundary and sufficient availability; neither is established.
hypotheses.equation: S_X = gamma_PV - (gamma_PX + gamma_XV); complete wetting is conditionally favored if S_X >= 0. gamma terms are interfacial free energies per area.

gaps.description: No cavity-resolved RNA identity/composition or boundary enrichment measurement, no relevant interfacial tensions, and no mapping from measured tie-line concentrations to internal image cavities. Thus the wetting condition and its causal relevance are wholly untested.

variables_units.f: dimensionless arithmetic mean of segmented per-droplet empty-area fractions at each time
variables_units.C_phase,i: RNA concentration of species i in phase, ng/uL, measured only at supplied tie-line endpoints
variables_units.Gamma_PV,Gamma_PX,Gamma_XV: interfacial free energies per area, units not supplied
variables_units.S_X: spreading coefficient, interfacial free energy per area
variables_units.E_X,boundary/E_X,adjacent: dimensionless ratio of species-X signal per calibrated area at boundary versus adjacent dense phase; proposed observable, not measured

equations: f(t) = (1/N(t)) sum_i q_i(t), where q_i is the segmented internal dark area divided by filled droplet area for droplet i; this is the supplied arithmetic mean convention.
S_X = gamma_PV - gamma_PX - gamma_XV; S_X >= 0 is the conditional complete-wetting criterion under the stated phase/interface convention. No gamma is measured.
Proposed discriminator: boundary enrichment ratio E_X,boundary/E_X,adjacent > 1 for interfacial adsorption; bulk-demixing alternative does not require this enrichment.
parameters_ranges: No physical parameter values/ranges available for interfacial energies, X abundance, adsorption, or wetting threshold.
Observed f values are between 0 and 1 by definition; do not use them as concentrations or fit an interfacial parameter from them.
initial_boundary_conditions: Observed starting f values are similar in A and B at 0 h; initial similarity alone does not establish identical latent composition or phase state.
No initial X abundance, cavity concentration, phase volume, or boundary condition is measured.
observation_mapping: Image segmentation maps each droplet to q_i and then the reported mean f; it provides no molecular identity or concentration calibration.
Phase endpoint assay maps separately measured tie-line samples to C_phase,i; it is not a time series or cavity-specific assay.
A decisive wetting test would measure calibrated X signal at cavity boundary and neighboring dense region in the same droplets, with RNA identity established independently.

alternatives.description: Cavity emerges from bulk compositional demixing or a local production/consumption gradient; a special boundary-affine X species is unnecessary.
alternatives.discriminator: Does not predict selective X enrichment at the cavity boundary as a necessary condition; it may still allow incidental enrichment.

alternatives.description: Amplification-associated carryover or another altered reaction condition changes transcription or phase behavior.
alternatives.discriminator: Could change f without the proposed X species being the boundary-active cause; no matched carryover control is supplied.

alternatives.description: Changing droplet population, track selection, or image thresholding contributes to the aggregate trajectory.
alternatives.discriminator: Current tracking lacks cavity state trajectories and cannot exclude this explanation.

predictions: Conditional prediction: if X-mediated wetting stabilizes cavities, boundary-to-adjacent-dense X enrichment should exceed one in cavity-bearing B droplets and should associate with persistence after controlling for local bulk X signal. This is not predicted as necessary by the bulk-demixing alternative.

A cavity-specific boundary enrichment result would support the bridge but would not by itself prove that X lowers interfacial free energy; direct perturbation or interfacial measurement would still be needed.
Absence of enrichment with a validated sensitive assay would weaken this specific wetting hypothesis while leaving bulk demixing and carryover explanations viable.
checks: Units: f and enrichment ratio are dimensionless; each gamma and S has interfacial-energy-per-area units, so the spreading-coefficient subtraction is dimensionally consistent.
Limit: if gamma_PV = gamma_PX + gamma_XV then S_X = 0, the marginal wetting boundary; if X is absent, the hypothesis reduces to no X-mediated effect.
Evidence does not identify X, quantify its RNA abundance, establish complete wetting, or close a mass balance.
No actual computation has been run in this reply.
evidence_conflicts: E02 supports a relationship between template-length fraction and endpoint f in separate preparations, but it does not establish an interfacial molecular mechanism.
E04 measures bulk coexisting-phase concentrations, not internal cavity contents; treating the dilute phase as the cavity would be an unsupported measurement equivalence.
Read frequencies are DNA measurements and cannot be used as RNA concentration fractions.
untested: Identity and transcription abundance of the putative X species.
Whether cavity persistence is within-droplet evolution rather than population/segmentation effects.
Whether amplification carryover or reaction conditions cause the phenotype.

T-L1-mechanism-bridge.deliverable: Evaluate whether preferential RNA boundary wetting is a coherent new bridge hypothesis; define phases/interfaces, derive a conditional boundary-enrichment prediction versus bulk demixing, and recommend the smallest discriminating measurement. Clearly separate supplied evidence, background relations, and new assumptions.
T-L1-mechanism-bridge.acceptance: No unmeasured tension, RNA identity, or concentration is presented as fact; no DNA-to-RNA abundance inference; formula and units checked; prediction has a distinct alternative; limits of E02/E04 are explicit.
T-L1-mechanism-bridge.reason: Prior rounds supplied descriptive kinetics, template-fraction endpoints, motion summaries and bulk tie-line endpoints but left the molecular connection to an internal cavity unobserved. This task targets that missing relation and yields a discriminating measurement rather than another time-only fit.

reply.recognition: I do not recognize a specific study with confidence.
reply.summary: Target quantity remains f(t), the arithmetic mean of per-droplet segmented internal dark-area fractions (dimensionless), not concentration or a phase volume fraction; initial evidence has two independent preparations per condition, with fields/objects nested. B rises from 0.01381 at 0 h to 0.08918 at 24 h while A declines from 0.01487 to about 0.0045. Existing evidence supports candidate heterogeneity (reference DNA read fraction 0.9466; listed other reads total 0.0500), endpoint differences among template-length fractions, and coexistence of reference/variant RNA concentrations in dilute and dense phases. It does not map RNA identity or phase composition to cavity interiors/boundaries, nor connect those endpoints causally to B. New explicitly hypothetical bridge: a minority RNA species generated from altered templates preferentially wets an internal RNA-poor/RNA-rich interface, lowering interfacial free energy and stabilizing a cavity after nucleation. For phases P (surrounding dense RNA) and V (cavity), complete wetting by species X requires the spreading coefficient S_X = gamma_PV - (gamma_PX + gamma_XV) >= 0 under the specified three-interface convention; this is an unmeasured condition, not a result. Distinct alternative: bulk demixing or local production/consumption creates a cavity without selective interfacial enrichment; it predicts no X enrichment at the boundary relative to adjacent dense phase. E04 partition ratios and E02 endpoint fractions do not estimate S_X or establish X as the sequenced variants. Task executor to assess whether the proposed interface bridge is scientifically coherent, derive its conditional observable prediction and compare it with bulk-demixing alternatives using only supplied evidence and eligible background. No computation or search has yet been performed.
